title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — 13.3.1 Grammar in Use: Word Class (Prepositions)

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Prepositions show where someone or something is, and which way they move. In this sub-strand you will find prepositions of position and direction in sentences about money, markets and banks, and you will use them so that a listener can find a person or a thing without guessing.

## Strand 13.0: Money
Sub-strand 13.3.1: Grammar in Use: Word Class (Prepositions)
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences
b) use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts
c) promote the use of prepositions for clarity in communication

## What this sub-strand covers
• Prepositions

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should we tell others exactly where people and things are?
2. How do we show the position of people and things?

## Core competencies
• Self-efficacy: The learner develops confidence and self-esteem when using prepositions correctly.
• Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with technology through watching videos and television programmes and seeing how people use prepositions in conversation.
• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner creates and displays charts featuring prepositions in the classroom.

## Values
• Love: It is achieved as the learner respects others’ work as created and displayed on preposition charts.
• Responsibility: The learner offers leadership and guidance to others while preparing to play appropriate preposition online and offline games.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Financial Literacy: This is realised when the learner interacts with materials about money as they watch videos about how people use money in their daily lives.
• Citizenship: This is nurtured as the learner learns about money and the importance of paying taxes to foster patriotism.

## Links to other learning areas
• The learner can link the content taught here to Social Studies where as a concept patriotism is promoted through sensitising learners about money and payment of tax.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 English Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Theme 13.0 Money, Sub-strand 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Prepositions of position and direction

LESSON 1: PREPOSITIONS OF POSITION AND DIRECTION
================================================

## What you will learn
• Name common prepositions of position and of direction.
• Find them in sentences.
• Match a preposition to the place or movement it describes.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences

## Introduction
If a friend says only 'The fee book is the office', you still do not know where to look. One small word, such as in, on or under, points you to the right place.

## Notes
### What a preposition does
A preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun to show position or direction. Position tells us where something is. Direction tells us which way it moves.

### Position
- in: inside something. The coins are in the tin.
- on: touching the top. The note is on the table.
- under: below and covered or lower. The book is under the register.
- above and below: higher than, or lower than, without having to touch. The shelf is above the desk. The mat is below the window.
- behind: at the back of. The bank is behind the market.
- in front of: at the face side of. The queue is in front of the stall.
- beside: at the side. The cashier stands beside the till.
- between: in the space separating two things. The coin rolled between the box and the wall.
- near: close to. The market is near the school.

### Direction
- to: movement towards a place. She walked to the bank.
- from: movement starting at a place. He came from the market.
- into: movement to the inside. She put the note into her pocket.
- out of: movement to the outside. He took a coin out of the tin.
- towards: in the direction of. The queue moved towards the stall.
- across: from one side to the other. They walked across the market.
- through: in one side and out the other. We went through the gate.
- up and down: to a higher or lower place. She went up the steps. The coin rolled down the slope.

### Spotting them
Read this report and find the prepositions.

'Asha put the fees in the box. The box is on the shelf behind the door. Then she walked to the office and gave the list to the teacher. A coin had fallen under the desk, so she picked it up and dropped it into the box.'

The prepositions are in, on, behind, to, under and into. In, on, behind and under show position. To and into show direction.

A picture test helps. If you can point to the place or trace the movement with your finger, you have understood the preposition.

## Key words
• preposition — a word that shows position or direction, such as in, on, to or from
• position — the place where someone or something is
• direction — the way someone or something moves
• till — a drawer or box where money is kept during buying and selling

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Is behind a preposition of position or of direction in 'The bank is behind the market'?

Working:
1. Ask whether something moves or stays.
2. The bank stays in a place.

Answer: Position. It tells us where the bank is.

### Example 2
Choose into or in: She dropped the coin ______ the tin.

Working:
1. The coin moves from outside to inside.
2. Into shows that movement. In would only say where it ended if we already knew it was there.

Answer: into

## Activity: Find and match
You will need: The report in the notes, A tin, a coin, a book and a desk, Paper for a chart
1. Underline the prepositions in the report and label each one position or direction.
2. One learner places the coin in, on, under or beside the tin. The partner says the sentence.
3. Then move the coin into the tin, out of the tin, or across the desk, and say the direction.
4. Start a chart with two columns, Position and Direction, and add the prepositions you used.

## Practice
1. List four prepositions of position and three of direction.
2. Where is the box in this sentence? The box is on the shelf behind the door.
3. Which word shows movement: the coin is in the tin, or she walked to the bank?
4. Fill the gap with between or beside: The cashier stands ______ the till, at its side.

## Summary
• Position prepositions say where something is.
• Direction prepositions say which way it moves.
• Into and out of show movement in or out. In and on show a place.

### Answers to practice
1. Examples: in, on, under, behind; to, from, into.
2. On the shelf, and the shelf is behind the door.
3. To, in the sentence 'She walked to the bank.'
4. beside

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Using prepositions so people can find things

LESSON 2: USING PREPOSITIONS SO PEOPLE CAN FIND THINGS
======================================================

## What you will learn
• Complete sentences with the preposition that matches the meaning.
• Write your own sentences about where money and people are.
• Explain why an exact preposition makes communication clearer.

Curriculum outcomes: b) use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts; c) promote the use of prepositions for clarity in communication

## Introduction
Two sentences can use the same nouns and still send a person to different places. 'The fees are in the cupboard' and 'The fees are on the cupboard' are not the same instruction. The preposition does the important work.

## Notes
### Choose, do not guess
Read the whole sentence and picture it before you pick the word.

The coins are ______ the locked tin. (in)
The receipt is ______ the counter. (on)
The parking sign is ______ the gate. (near, beside or in front of, if that is the picture)
She took the change ______ her pocket. (out of)
We walked ______ the market to the bank. (from)

A substitution table lets you try several words and keep only the true one.

The money is ______ the box. — in / on / under / behind

Only one of those is true for a given picture. Say the sentence aloud. If you cannot point to the place, change the preposition.

### Write your own
Use this frame: person or thing + verb + preposition + place.

- The salary book is in the office.
- Hassan walked from the stall to the gate.
- The note slipped between the pages.
- Amina stood in front of the class and counted the coins.

Keep the noun after the preposition. We do not say 'She walked to' and stop. To needs a place: to the bank.

### Why exactness matters
Money is easy to misplace, and people waiting in a market need clear directions. 'It is somewhere near' wastes time. 'It is in the blue tin under the desk' can be checked at once. The same care helps when you give directions to a visitor or explain where you left a book.

Using prepositions well is a way of respecting the listener. You imagine what they can see, and you give them the word that matches the real place or the real movement. A class chart of prepositions, with a small drawing beside each word, keeps the meanings in view while you write.

## Key words
• receipt — a note that shows what was paid
• substitution — trying one word in place of another in the same frame
• frame — a sentence pattern you can complete with your own words

## Worked examples

### Example 1
The picture shows a coin under a book. Complete: The coin is ______ the book.

Working:
1. The coin is lower than the book and covered by it.
2. Under matches that position.

Answer: under

### Example 2
Correct the unfinished sentence: Mother walked to.

Working:
1. To is a preposition and needs a place after it.

Answer: Example: Mother walked to the market.

## Activity: Preposition chart and gap sentences
You will need: Manila paper, Pictures or classroom objects, Gap sentences on the board
1. In groups, complete six gap sentences about a market or a fee tin. Agree on the preposition only when everyone can point to the place or the movement.
2. Play a game: one learner hides a coin in, on, under or behind an object. The others ask, 'Is it under the book?' until they find it.
3. Make a chart with a drawing for at least six prepositions and display it.
4. Each learner writes four sentences of their own using four different prepositions.

## Practice
1. Choose in or on: The coins are locked ______ the tin. The tin is ______ the table.
2. Complete: We walked ______ the market ______ the school gate. (from, to)
3. Why is 'The fees are in the blue tin' clearer than 'The fees are somewhere'?
4. Write a sentence with between about two coins and a book.

## Summary
• Picture the place or the movement before you choose the preposition.
• A preposition needs a noun after it.
• Exact prepositions help people find things and follow directions.

### Answers to practice
1. The coins are locked in the tin. The tin is on the table.
2. We walked from the market to the school gate.
3. The preposition and the place tell the listener exactly where to look.
4. Example: The bookmark is between the two coins. Or: One coin rolled between the book and the tin.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 13.3.1 GRAMMAR IN USE: WORD CLASS (PREPOSITIONS)
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which word is a preposition of position?
   A. quickly
   B. under
   C. count
   D. honest

2. Which word is a preposition of direction?
   A. beside
   B. into
   C. above
   D. near

3. The bank is behind the market. Behind tells us
   A. the price
   B. the position
   C. the date
   D. the owner's name

4. She put the note ______ her pocket. The note moves inside.
   A. into
   B. above
   C. beside
   D. between

5. The coin is covered by the book, lower than it. The coin is ______ the book.
   A. on
   B. under
   C. towards
   D. across

6. Which sentence is complete?
   A. He walked from the market to the bank.
   B. He walked from.
   C. He walked to.
   D. He from the market walked to.

7. The cashier stands at the side of the till. Choose the preposition.
   A. beside
   B. through
   C. into
   D. down

8. Why do we tell someone exactly where a fee tin is?
   A. So they can find it without guessing
   B. So the sentence has no verb
   C. So we can hide the tin
   D. So prepositions can be left out

9. What is the difference between in and into?

10. Write a sentence that uses both from and to.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 13.3.1 GRAMMAR IN USE: WORD CLASS (PREPOSITIONS)
========================================

1. B. under
   Under tells us where something is.

2. B. into
   Into shows movement to the inside. The others show position.

3. B. the position
   Behind gives the position of the bank.

4. A. into
   Into shows movement to the inside.

5. B. under
   Under matches a lower, covered position.

6. A. He walked from the market to the bank.
   From and to each have a place after them.

7. A. beside
   Beside means at the side.

8. A. So they can find it without guessing
   An exact preposition saves time and confusion.

9. In shows position inside something. Into shows movement from outside to inside.
   Position and direction are different jobs.

10. Example: Asha walked from the stall to the bank.
   From marks the start and to marks the place she went towards.
